transcript:
Meeting: POC weekly sync - dedicated sizing & autoscale
Date: 2025-11-17
Time: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Evan Cruz (Redwood SE), Liam Brooks (Redwood CSM), Sofia Kim (NovaFin Head of ML), Raj Patel (NovaFin Infra Lead), Elena Morales (NovaFin Security)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick agenda — we want to review last week's perf runs, talk autoscale thresholds, burst pool sizing, and confirm next steps.
[00:18] Sofia: Yep thanks. We did a couple of runs friday, mostly p50/p95 look okay but we saw cost spike during bursts.
[00:30] Evan: Right, and the kv cache hit was about 42% on the long prompt suite which contributed to higher token churn.
[00:45] Raj: Just to add, our infra limits are a hard egress cap in the east region, so we want to avoid huge concurrent spikes unless you have a local region plan.
[01:05] Liam: Noted — we'll keep that in mind for burst planning.
[01:20] Maya: Quick numbers recap from the Friday run: sustained throughput at 120 req/s for the short-chat model, p50 latency ~110ms, p95 ~420ms. Burst test to 300 req/s showed p95 degradation to ~1.2s and GPU utilization hit 98% on one node.
[01:45] Sofia: 1.2s p95 during burst is acceptable for some flows but our real-time quoting endpoint needs <700ms p95.
[02:00] Evan: We think two levers — bump the Dedicated pool to add a small burst capacity (we call it burst pool), and tune autoscale to proactively spin up nodes at 65% GPU util vs the default 80%. That reduces cold starts.
[02:20] Raj: How does that affect cost? If we keep an idle burst pool, that's committed spend right?
[02:35] Maya: Burst pool can be configured as reserved but billed only when used if you pair with capacity credits — there's a blend. We'll send numbers but expect a ~12-18% incremental uplift for the sizes we're discussing vs baseline.
[02:55] Sofia: Can you explain the autoscale policy options? We liked the idea of dual-metric scaling (GPU util + queue length).
[03:10] Evan: Sure. We recommend GPU utilization for throughput-bound workloads, queue length for latency-sensitive peaks. Example: lower threshold to 60% GPU util with queue-length trigger at 10 reqs gives earlier scale-outs. Also warm-start by keeping one min node warm for the heavy models.
[03:40] Raj: For warm nodes, do you have suggestions to avoid memory leak / kv cache growth?
[03:50] Evan: Yes, set a config to recycle warm nodes every 6-12 hours depending on memory drift and use shorter kv cache TTL for endpoints that share variable prompts.
[04:10] Elena: On the security side, what changes with a burst pool — especially regarding audit logs and key usage? We need KMS separation and audit trails.
[04:25] Maya: Burst nodes are part of the Dedicated tenant and use the same KMS integration; we can map separate key aliases for burst pool and provide per-node audit logs. We'll share the SOC2 and KMS docs after this call.
[04:40] Elena: Also confirm network segmentation — VPC peering and allowed CIDR ranges.
[04:48] Evan: We'll include the VPC setup recipe and recommended firewall rules in the doc pack.
[05:00] Sofia: Looking at the token distribution — long-form summarization endpoints are the heavy tail. Can quantization help here without quality regressions?
[05:15] Evan: For large models, int8 quantization helps reduce GPU memory which allows more concurrent inferences; quality impact is minimal for summarization but we should run evals on your prompt set. We did a quick ablation Friday and saw negligible ROUGE drop on the short-suite but will run your full eval.
[05:40] Raj: If we quantize, does that force a model variant change in the POC?
[05:48] Evan: It creates a compatible quantized variant; runtime supports fallback to full-precision if needed. We also support routing policies so sensitive endpoints can hit full-precision.
[06:05] Maya: Back to capacity: given your peak 5-min rolling rate last week was ~250 req/s with 70% of requests being short-chat, our initial recommendation is a Dedicated baseline of 4 nodes (A100-equivalent) with a burst pool of 2 nodes and autoscale min=2, max=8, scale-up at 60% GPU or queue>8.
[06:30] Sofia: That sounds reasonable. Can you give the expected p95 for the quoting endpoint under that config?
[06:38] Evan: We project 500-650ms p95 for quoting if we reserve the warm node and use aggressive queue-based scale. We'll validate in the 24h stress.
[06:50] Raj: What's the plan for canarying the burst? We need to avoid tripping our egress caps.
[07:00] Liam: Proposed canary: route 2% of production traffic through Redwood Dedicated for 48 hours with a traffic cap; monitor egress & latency. If green, increase to 10% and then full.
[07:15] Sofia: We also want improved observability — token-level cost per route and model-level traces.
[07:25] Maya: Console supports token-level cost breakdown and per-route dashboards; we can add custom tracing hooks for your request IDs. We'll include config steps.
[07:40] Elena: About compliance, we need proof of SOC2 Type II, penetration test summary, and KMS/HSM attestations.
[07:50] Maya: We'll send the certs and the signed attestation. If you need vendor-specific paperwork, tell us which fields in the questionnaire are blocking and we'll prioritize.
[08:05] Raj: On autoscale cooldowns — what's recommended? We saw oscillation in earlier POC where nodes flapped.
[08:15] Evan: Increase scale-down cooldown to 6 minutes and use percent-based scaling rather than single-node steps; also use predictive scaler based on moving-average of queue length for smoothing.
[08:35] Sofia: Can Redwood run the 24h run with our exact traffic shape? That will be most useful.
[08:42] Evan: Yes, we can. We'll need the 7-day histogram and ideal SLOs from you. We'll drop the run artifacts and a spreadsheet with CPU/GPU util and per-endpoint latencies.
[09:00] Maya: Next, pricing — we'll provide a sample cost model for baseline vs baseline+burst and include committed discounts for a 6- or 12-month reserved pool.
[09:12] Raj: Any blockers from your side instrumenting the traffic? We use tokenized logs in S3 with gz format.
[09:20] Evan: We can ingest S3 gz logs; a small ingestion script required but we can share. Alternatively, you can paste a small sample CSV.
[09:30] Sofia: For the evals, please run the ROUGE and BLEU suites and also our internal QA prompts — we'll share the list.
[09:40] Evan: Got it. We'll include model-variant comparisons (fp16 vs int8) and the impact on latency/cost.
[09:50] Liam: I'll schedule a follow-up next week same time to review the 24h run results. Tentative for 11/24 at 10am PST.
[10:02] Elena: One more security note — we need retention policies for logs and the ability to purge per retention window.
[10:10] Maya: We support configurable retention and per-tenant purge requests; we'll include the procedure.
[10:18] Sofia: Okay sounds good. Quick recap?
[10:22] Maya: Recap: Redwood runs 24h stress with burst pattern (Evan), share pricing (Maya), NovaFin provides logs and SLOs (Sofia/Raj), security docs exchanged (Elena). Follow-up 11/24 to review.
[10:35] Raj: That covers it from infra. Thanks.
[10:38] Everyone: Thanks, bye.

Notes: transcription contains minor speaker attribution/typos; some technical terms abbreviated (kv cache as kvcache), occasional overlaps. Links referenced: "redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf" (to be shared), "novafin-traffic-histogram.csv" (customer to provide), "redwood-soc2-kms.zip" (to be shared).
